text:
alex: FYI filing the postmortem follow-up here — last night's KV-cache OOM on inference-rc1. Root PM notes + immediate mitigation steps in the doc, but we need tracked owners for remediation and a timeline.

maria: thanks. quick recap: OOM triggered after a long-tail chat session where the per-session KV cache grew with no eviction; host ran out of RSS and cgroup killed process. we saw jemalloc fragmentation spike in the minutes prior.

raj: attaching link to heap dumps in s3: s3://redwood-debug/1742009876/gcore.tgz and jemalloc stats at s3://redwood-debug/1742009876/jemalloc.txt :thumbsup:

emily: I pulled the jemalloc stats — fragmentation ratio ~1.45, active/allocated drifted up during the 90m window. also saw many small allocations (~64-512b churn) from tokenizer cache.

kevin: is this the recurring pattern we've seen in feb/mar incidents or a new vector?

alex: it's similar to 172... incident (long sessions + repeated streaming) but differs: earlier incidents had a leak in response buffers; this looks like KV entries never being pruned. not identical but repeating pattern of long-lived sessions + no eviction.

maria: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) set hard per-session KV limit (default 50MB) + reject/trim requests that exceed it; 2) enable periodic KV trimming background job every 5m; 3) deploy jemalloc opt to reduce fragmentation (config change).

raj: agree. I can do (1) and (2) — will open infra PR to add config + runtime enforcement in session manager. ETA: Wed COB.

emily: I'll run memprof on a repro locally and generate a focused flamegraph + allocation heatmap. can we get a repro script that simulates long chat with repeated tool calls?

alex: raj, can you drop steps to repro in the ticket? emily needs the workload.

raj: on it — will add a k6 script and recorded session payloads. also will include cgroup-limited run so we can reproduce OOM behavior.

kevin: who will own validating the jemalloc config change and making sure it doesn't regress latency? that's typically performance infra.

maria: performance infra -> kevin. suggested jemalloc flags: "background_thread:true, decay_time:0" (to reduce retention) and try experimental "opt.retain:false". we'll test perf impact in staging.

kevin: ok I'll run A/B with canary and collect p50/p95 p99 and memory RSS trends. plan: canary -> 25% traffic -> 2h -> metrics. ETA for canary: Thu morning.

alex: good. we also need observability improvements (alerts + dashboards):
- alert if per-session KV exceeds 40MB for >2m
- chart fragmentation ratio (jemalloc: allocated/active) per host
- histogram of session durations vs KV size

emily: I'll add the dashboard tiles and alert rules. will link to Grafana dashboard when done. ETA: Tue EOD.

raj: one more thing: backend GC/trimming API. we should add an admin endpoint to forcibly trim KV caches on a given instance (useful for mitigation while code changes roll out). I can add a small RPC.

maria: ownership summary so we don't lose track:
- raj: implement per-session KV hard limit + periodic trimming job + repro script (ETA Wed COB)
- kevin: jemalloc config testing and canary rollout (ETA Thu 25% canary)
- emily: profiling + flamegraphs + Grafana dashboards and alert rules (ETA Tue EOD)
- alex: coordinate postmortem follow-ups, verify fixes, and lead incident review next week (ETA: follow-up review Fri)

kevin: addendum: I'll also validate GC/allocator symbols are available for pprof, and if not, enable debug builds for staging canary.

sre-bot: incident counter updated: INC-2026-03-22-12 -> follow-ups created: TASK-5248 (raj), TASK-5249 (kevin), TASK-5250 (emily), TASK-5251 (alex).

alex: timeline check — we should aim to ship the hard limit + trimming + alerting this week. jemalloc tunings can be canaried next week if needed. if short-term mitigations are sufficient, we can avoid emergency capacity bump.

maria: decision: implement hard limit + trimming + alerting asap; if canary shows fragmentation persists, escalate to allocator change and capacity bump as backup.

emily: I'll add regression tests to the eval harness to run a 2h long session at scale daily to detect recurrence. linking test -> TASK-5252.

raj: PR #6829 opened for session-manager limit + trimming job. marking as WIP. includes feature flag.

kevin: created k8s canary manifest with jemalloc env and 25% rollout. PR #6837.

alex: great. final ask: raj/kevin/emily — please post short status updates in this thread when you hit your milestones so we can close the loop during the postmortem review.

maria: thanks everyone. tagging infra-oncall to be aware of the mitigation windows. :handshake:

raj: FYI added commands for local repro in the ticket:
```
# simulate 200 sessions with long streams
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 2h kv_long_stream.js
# collect jemalloc stats
curl http://localhost:9000/debug/jemalloc > jemalloc.txt
# heap dump
gcore $(pidof inference_service) && tar -czf gcore.tgz core.*
```

emily: got the scripts, starting profiling now. will post flamegraphs to s3://redwood-debug/1742009876/profiles when done.

alex: closing the loop: we'll review at the Friday incident follow-up and confirm owners moved tasks to done. if any blocker, escalate to oncall. thanks all.

kevin: quick note—if anyone sees immediate OOM risk on prod, put instance pool into maintenance and scale up dedicated hosts. don't wait for canary if risk high.

maria: noted. adding runbook step to incident playbook.

sre-bot: tasks updated: TASK-5248 -> in_progress, TASK-5249 -> review, TASK-5250 -> in_progress, TASK-5252 -> queued

alex: perfect. that's it for now.
